correctness.rationale: For all fixed b,r>=2 with gamma=b(r-1)-r>=1, a common saturated bj-set has exact expected count Qj; a three-regime binomial and Stirling entropy bound proves sum_(j>=2) Qj=O(n^(-2gamma)). Exact first and second factorial moments for common b-blocks sandwich noncollapse probability at mu+O(n^(-2gamma)). Excluding multiple common blocks and larger components yields conditional two-class concentration with 1-O(n^(-gamma)). Independent alternating-cycle counting treats (2,2); a component-rooting decomposition gives the exact recurrence. The extracted stand-alone finite checker exhaustively verified eleven small cases and the moment/recurrence identities; the infinite proof is mathematical, not a finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The candidate is a sharp fixed-width modal-algebra identity law with its leading constant, O(n^(-2gamma)) absolute remainder and conditional rare-failure shape, not merely qualitative connectivity. Full-text and indexed comparisons did not identify a statement implying these conclusions in the *independent uniform equal-block partition* law. Unrestricted Bell partitions, prescribed-permutation-cycle transitivity and simple regular hypergraphs are scientifically adjacent but differently sampled or qualitatively weaker. The exceptional two-perfect-matching calculation is expressly not offered as original. Earlier broader results remain a documented historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier general result for transitivity of independent random conjugacy-class elements or colored hypergraph configurations might imply a relative asymptotic or conditional small-orbit law; historical priority is not independently certified.
The primary MSC follows the common-knowledge modal-operator identity; related hypergraph and permutation-group formulations cross into other MSC categories.
The finite checker tests exact combinatorial identities only at small parameter values; the asymptotic proof is analytic.

value.rationale: A fixed uniform information-class size is a natural finite epistemic resource. The sharp asymptotic probability and conditional unique small knowledge component give a complete b,r fixed-parameter characterization of when the common-knowledge box equals universal box on all valuations. The power-law exponent and exact constant are mathematically nontrivial, with a distinguished two-matching boundary and an exact finite count recurrence. This goes beyond a qualitative zero–one statement, a relabeling of a prior theorem, or an arbitrary numerical table.
